Contribution.text: Wasmtime's 24.0.0 release has been retroactively classified as a LTS release and will be supported until August 20, 2026. Wasmtime’s upcoming 36.0.0 release on August 20, 2025 will be supported until August 20, 2027, meaning that users will have one year starting in August to upgrade from 24.0.0 to 36.0.0. Wasmtime 34.0.0, to be released June 20, 2025, will be supported up until the release of Wasmtime 36.0.0 on August 20, 2025. Each release that is a multiple of 12 is considered an LTS release and is supported for 24 months. Other releases are supported for 2 months. Every 12th version of Wasmtime will now be considered an LTS release and will receive security fixes for 2 years, or 24 months.

research.notes: No deterministic source exists: endoflife.date has no Wasmtime product (475 products, no wasm identity), and the vendor's own lifecycle table at docs.wasmtime.dev/stability-release.html ships an empty static tbody -- every Version/Branch Date/Release Date/EOL Date row is produced in the browser by docs/js/index.js as 2024-04-20 plus (n-20) months, with +24 months for LTS and +2 months for normal releases. That is duration arithmetic, never a published date, so no collector is admissible. Dates here are the vendor's own explicit day-precision statements. Only releases the announcement itself dates are given dates: 24.0.0 (LTS, end of support 2026-08-20), 36.0.0 (LTS, 2025-08-20 to 2027-08-20), and 34.0.0, the one non-LTS line the notice ends explicitly (2025-08-20, at 36.0.0's release). 48.0.0 is the current LTS (released 2026-08-20) and carries no dates: the announcement predates it and publishes no deadline for it, so none is inferred. The remaining non-LTS branches (25-47) are governed only by the 2-month duration policy quoted below; that policy is stored as evidence and is never converted into a date, so those lines are not published with invented ends. ga for 24.0.0 and 48.0.0 stays null because no stored quote states it. Rendering defect: the live article page ends the 24.0.0 sentence at "until August 20," because the following "2026." was consumed as an ordered-list marker, so that one sentence is cited to the vendor's own published source file for the article rather than to the rendered page. Category framework follows the runtime precedent: endoflife.date categorizes the comparable runtimes nodejs, deno and bun as framework.
